subject: Post-demo: BrightPark throughput & budget scan
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Thomas Lee <thomas.lee@brightpark.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 18 Nov 2026 15:02:00 -0800
Subject: Post-demo: BrightPark throughput & budget scan

Thanks again for taking the demo today, Thomas — great to see how BrightPark plans to route user queries through a single inference tier. Quick recap and a few asks so we can run preliminary sizing + cost math: 

1) Expected monthly tokens (best guess): you mentioned an initial rollout to ~50k monthly active users with an average of ~650 tokens per active user per month — that maps to ~32.5M tokens/month. Can you confirm if that aligns with your product metrics?

2) Peak TPS window: you called out short spikes during morning syncs — can you quantify the 1-minute peak TPS you expect? You gave a range on the call but I want a single conservative number to run a hosted SLO simulation.

3) Traffic shape & burst tolerance: please attach a sample day (CSV) with minute granularity if possible. That will let us test batching and concurrency profiles.

4) Budget target: what is your target $/1M tokens (ballpark)? If you have a monthly budget range for hosted inference that we should aim to respect, please share.

I attached a tiny sample CSV template (brightpark_traffic_sample.csv) — drop your real numbers into that and reply. Karthik, looping you for a quick sanity-check on the traffic assumptions and to run an initial pricing sketch once we get the CSV.

Next steps: Thomas to share the CSV + budget window; we’ll return a short hosted pricing sketch and a peak TPS SLO/latency tradeoff table by EOD Friday.

Best,
Jordan
Jordan Blake
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
https://redwood.ai

Attachments: brightpark_traffic_sample.csv (CSV - 2KB)
From: Thomas Lee <thomas.lee@brightpark.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Platform Team <infra@brightpark.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 19 Nov 2026 09:18:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: BrightPark throughput & budget scan

Jordan — thanks for the clear notes. Attach is a representative weekday (minute-level) and a short summary:

- Current daily MAU (pilot target): ~50k active users across web + mobile.
- Average tokens per user/month: ~650 (this includes prompt + completion tokens after our truncation rules).
- Monthly tokens (expected pilot): ~32.5M (agree with your calc).
- Peak minute: we see brief peaks ~1.8 qps/user across a cohort leading to ~750 TPS (1-minute peak).
- Sustained hour-long peaks are more like 280 TPS.
- Budget: initial pilot has a soft cap of $3k - $6k/month for hosted inference (we know it’s tight).

Sending the CSV now (see attached brightpark_traffic_sample.csv). If you could run a hosted estimate that assumes 99th percentile latency <= 400ms and show the unit $/1M for both standard and aggressive batching profiles that would be ideal.

—Thomas
Thomas Lee
Head of Platform, BrightPark
thomas.lee@brightpark.com

Attachments: brightpark_traffic_sample.csv (CSV - 56KB)
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Thomas Lee <thomas.lee@brightpark.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:34:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: BrightPark throughput & budget scan

Perfect, Thomas — got the CSV and numbers, thanks. Quick clarifications before Karthik runs numbers: 

- The 750 TPS is a 1-minute peak (short spikes) — is that a single region / single endpoint or spread across three regions? You wrote earlier that web clients are US-west primarily but mobile fans are global. For a hosted SLO we need region split.
- The 280 TPS sustained hour: is that likely to repeat daily (e.g., a 1-hour window every morning), or only occasional?

If you don’t have region splits, we’ll run a conservative single-region calc for US-west which will give an upper-bound to cost. Karthik — if those numbers hold I’ll hand this to you to produce: 
  * Simple hosted estimate with $/1M tokens for two profiles (standard batching vs aggressive batching with 2–3x latency tradeoff).
  * Peak capacity sizing to meet 99th <= 400ms for the standard profile (assume model = redwood/gpt-med-1 and default quantization).
  * A second column showing potential savings if BrightPark is ok with 50–100ms additional tail latency for the aggressive batching case.

I’ll plan to share a short PDF quote (redwood_quote_v2.pdf) after we pick the profile — aiming EOD Monday.

Jordan
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Thomas Lee <thomas.lee@brightpark.com>
Date: Sat, 21 Nov 2026 11:24:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Post-demo: BrightPark throughput & budget scan

Thanks for the data — ran a quick back-of-envelope and a couple of observations: 

- Monthly tokens: 32.5M — base unit cost scenarios (hosted) 
  • Standard batching: ~$12.50 / 1M tokens => ~$406/month (tokens only)
  • Aggressive batching (higher efficiency): ~$8.25 / 1M tokens => ~$268/month

- Peak sizing: to sustain 750 TPS 1-minute peak under standard profile (99th <= 400ms) we estimate a need for ~2 concurrent inference shards in our hosted pool (with autoscale headroom). If BrightPark wants single-region redundancy to handle AZ failure, add one more shard — we’ll show that in the formal quote.

- If your pilot budget is $3k–$6k/month, either profile fits comfortably at pilot scale (even when adding network & egress, SLO margin, and some ingress overhead). The savings delta matters more at 10s-100s of millions of tokens.

Next steps from me: I’ll produce the two-profile table + an annotated cost worksheet and share a short PDF by EOD Monday. Jordan — confirm if we should assume US-west single-region run for the conservative quote. Thomas — if you want multi-region split now, say how you’d like traffic distributed and I’ll re-run.

-Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
karthik.iyer@redwood.ai

Attachments referenced: redwood_quote_v2.pdf (will follow), brightpark_traffic_sample.csv
